title: A Choir for the Sigil
premise: Vesper Pemberton, the last swordspeaker whose oaths can bind reality itself, has hidden for five years in the magic-outlawed city of Greyhollow, selling harmless charms and denying their gift. When a dying courier presses a map into Vesper's hands—a map to the court beneath the mountain where souls are sold as currency—they learn the soul it leads to belongs to Wren, a street musician Vesper secretly loves, whose voice was traded to pay her family's debts. Pursued by the Magistrate's witch-hunters and shadowed by the courier's vengeful ghost, Vesper must choose between the oath of silence that keeps them safe and the older, truer oath of the swordspeakers: that no soul is property. In the court beneath the mountain, Vesper challenges the Soul-Broker to a speaking-duel, wins Wren's voice back at the cost of their own magic, and returns to a Greyhollow where they finally belong—not as the last of something dying, but as the first of something new.
about_author: Yara Coldharbour is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing other people's justice before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town famous for its fog, where they sing alto in a community choir that rehearses above a shuttered apothecary.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet Greyhollow in deepening autumn: Vesper sells luck-knots and fever-salves from a market stall, carefully mundane, while witch-hunters patrol with iron bells. A routine inspection nearly exposes them when a charm hums at Vesper's touch. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of hiding, and the ache of watching Wren sing in the square—music Vesper can never join.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The dying courier Bramble collapses into Vesper's shop at midnight, pursued by something unseen. With his last breath he presses a bloodstained map into Vesper's hands and speaks an old swordspeaker's phrase—the challenge-oath no one has used in twenty years. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant recognition; the past Vesper buried has found them anyway.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Say
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with a haunting interlude from Bramble's ghost. The map only reveals its route when spoken aloud in true oath-tongue—forcing Vesper to use their outlawed gift for the first time in five years. Each spoken line makes the magic louder, more audible to hunters. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, frightening return of power, and guilt over Bramble's death.

chapters.title: The Voice That Was Sold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, mute since midsummer, communicates through chalkboards and songless humming, hiding the shame of what she traded to save her brother from debtors' prison. She recognizes the map's sigil—she signed it herself, in the Broker's parlor beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: grief, self-blame, and the fierce love that will make her follow Vesper rather than be protected.

chapters.title: Iron Bells at Dawn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Witch-hunter Captain Serane Ovid traces the oath-magic's echo to Vesper's door. Vesper and Wren flee through Greyhollow's flooded undercity with Bramble's ghost as unwilling guide, who demands they avenge him on the Broker. Emotional beat: fugitive intimacy—two people stripped of pretense, discovering trust in motion.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Frostline
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On the mountain road, the party shelters with a hidden enclave of surviving hedge-witches who recognize Vesper's oath-mark. They reveal the truth: the Magistrate didn't outlaw magic—he monopolized it, feeding condemned souls to the Broker to buy the city's unnatural prosperity. Emotional beat: belonging glimpsed and immediately threatened; Vesper learns their exile was engineered.

chapters.title: Serane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The hunter catches them at a frozen pass but hesitates—her own sister's soul was sold years ago. She offers passage in exchange for proof of her sister's fate, knowing treason. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as fellow prisoner; duty cracking against love, mirroring Vesper's own conflict.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Descending through singing tunnels, they reach the Broker's mirrored court, where shelves of glass vessels hold murmuring souls—including Serane's sister and hundreds of Greyhollow's 'executed.' The Broker offers Vesper everything: restoration, safety, Wren's voice—in exchange for the map and their silence forever. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive, because every offer is real.

chapters.title: The Speaking-Duel
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, climax. Vesper invokes the challenge-oath before the whole court. Words become weapons; the duel strips away Vesper's memories of hiding, of Wren, threatening to leave them hollow even in victory. At the brink, Wren sings wordlessly—and the sound of unowned music shatters the Broker's claim that souls can be sold at all. The vessels break; the mountain exhales five years of stolen voices. Emotional beat: sacrifice answered by love; the law of the court undone by a higher law.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Sigil
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, resolution. Vesper wakes magic-less but remembered, held by Wren whose voice has returned. In Greyhollow, the exposed Magistrate falls; Serane rebuilds the hunt into a protection for the gifted. On the first day of true winter, a choir gathers in the square—witches, hunters, freed voices, and Vesper, who cannot sing but conducts. Emotional beat: quiet joy; belonging not granted but built.
